## Existing Patterns & Conventions
- Setup mutants must sit beside the real script (`tests/smoke.sh:5425-5429`, `l3_su_mut`), or the root is untrusted and the mutation passes vacuously.
- Sub-suites are sourced from `tests/smoke.sh:6703-6710` (`. "$REPO/tests/smoke-<part>.sh"`), each with its own `x_fail` and a closing `ok "…; N mutations caught"`.
- Errors carry the evidence: setup's `die` names the file and says "nothing was written" (`hooks/hefesto-setup.sh:66`).
- jq does the merge in one program over `$CUR` (`:302-355`); bash builds the rule arrays (`:120-142`).
- Constitution 3: every guard mutation-tested; constitution "the matcher performs no expansion" — rules mirror the command byte for byte.

## External facts (Claude Code permissions doc, code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, read 2026-11-09)
- Evaluation order deny → ask → allow; a matching ask prompts even when a more specific allow matches; holds in auto mode, and for any subcommand of a compound command.
- `*` anywhere stands for any text; `:*` only at the end; a trailing ` *` matches the bare command only when it is the only wildcard.
- PreToolUse hook decisions do not bypass ask rules.
- Rules match the text Claude writes after stripping `timeout|time|nice|nohup|stdbuf|command|builtin`; `bash <path>` is not stripped.
